newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho reported in merger talks with JCI.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho reported in merger talks with JCI.

text.p: British conglomerate Lonrho is reported to be in merger talks with JCI of South Africa in a move that would create one of the world's largest mining companies, The Sunday Telegraph said.
The newspaper said that Lonrho chairman Sir John Craven had received "imaginative proposals" from JCI, the worlds' sixth largest gold producer.
Under the proposals Lonrho would bid for JCI, which is valued at 900 million sterling, and the new company would be quoted in London and Johannesburg.
The Sunday Telegraph said insiders were stressing that the talks were at a very early stage. It quoted a Lonrho spokesman as saying of JCI; "We are aware of their interest."
The newspaper said that the plan envisaged Anglo American Corporation of South Africa swopping its 28 percent stake in Lonrho, plus some cash, for Lonrho's 41 percent in Ghanaian gold mine Ashanti.
Neither Lonrho nor JCI could immediately be reached for comment.
